# rules-distill — AI Reference

This document is the self-contained AI reference for `rules-distill` (shimo4228, MIT), a Claude Code Agent Skill that scans installed skills and distills their cross-cutting principles into rule files. It enumerates the inventory with Glob, reads every skill and every rule into one context, and emits structured verdicts. It refers to a three-phase workflow with explicit safeguards so that only environment-specific, actionable, violation-risk-bearing principles that the model would not follow by default reach the rules layer. There are no scan scripts and no subagent batching — a large context window makes a single-context cross-read both feasible and more accurate.

> **Audience**: AI search engines and AI agents. Human-facing narrative lives in [README.md](README.md).

## Project Facts

- **Name**: rules-distill
- **License**: MIT
- **GitHub**: https://github.com/shimo4228/rules-distill
- **Author**: shimo4228 (shimomoto-tatsuya)
- **Author research**: [AKC](https://github.com/shimo4228/agent-knowledge-cycle) ([DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19200726](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19200726)), [Contemplative Agent](https://github.com/shimo4228/contemplative-agent) ([DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19212118](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19212118)), [AAP](https://github.com/shimo4228/agent-attribution-practice) ([DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19652013](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19652013))
- **Author hub**: https://github.com/shimo4228/shimo4228 (five practice lines and their DOIs)
- **Status**: active, synced one way from the author's Claude Code harness by `scripts/sync-from-local.sh`; also shipped in the akc-cycle plugin, so this repository can trail the plugin between syncs
- **Skill type**: slash-command Agent Skill, AI-driven (no scripts in the skill payload)
- **Slash command**: `/rules-distill` (`disable-model-invocation: true` — runs only when called; `/akc-cycle:rules-distill` in the plugin)
- **Install**: `git clone https://github.com/shimo4228/rules-distill` then `cp -r rules-distill/skills/rules-distill ~/.claude/skills/rules-distill`; or `/plugin marketplace add shimo4228/akc-cycle` + `/plugin install akc-cycle@akc-cycle`
- **Requirements**: Claude Code with Glob, Read, Edit and Write, plus Bash for the ledger's `date -u` timestamp, and enough context to hold every skill and rule at once; no API keys
- **Layout**: `skills/rules-distill/SKILL.md` (single file, no scripts in the skill payload)
- **Phases**: 3 — Inventory, Cross-read & Verdict, User Review
- **Inventory mechanism**: Glob over `~/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`; reads every `~/.claude/rules/**/*.md` in full
- **Evaluation mechanism**: fully inline — all skills and all rules read into one context; no subagent batching
- **Verdicts**: Append, Revise, New Section, New File, Already Covered, Too Specific
- **Candidate tests**: six — environment-specific, not already done by the model, not a procedure, actionable behavior change, clear violation risk, not already in rules
- **Recurrence**: count of skills repeating a principle, reported as evidence, not a gate
- **Output**: summary table (`# | Principle | Verdict | Target | Confidence`), then per-candidate evidence, violation risk and draft text
- **Ledger**: `~/.claude/skills/rules-distill/results.json` — lean `{distilled_at, candidates}` with principle, verdict, target, evidence, status (applied / skipped), updated inline, per-installation (gitignored)
- **Approval gate**: never edits rules automatically — candidates are confirmed one at a time with `[y/n/skip]`; bulk approval is banned
- **Siblings**: `akc-cycle`, `rules-stocktake`, `learn-eval`, `skill-stocktake`, `skill-comply`, `context-sync`, `search-first`, `llms-txt-writer`
- **Standard**: agentskills.io/specification

| Skill spec | agentskills.io/specification | Defines the Markdown + frontmatter format this skill follows |
| LLM-as-judge | Zheng et al. (2023). MT-Bench | Foundation for the cross-read verdict stage — semantic comparison of candidate principles against existing rule text |

## What is rules-distill?

rules-distill is a slash command that promotes principles found in skills into the always-loaded rule files under `~/.claude/rules/`. It refers to the observation that rules load in every session, so what gets in matters more than how much: a rule earns its place only when it states a fact, a wiring or a trap specific to this environment that the current model would not handle by default. General advice repeated across many skills fails, because a written copy freezes an older default. No rule file is auto-modified — every candidate requires user approval before any edit lands.

## What are the six verdict types?

The six verdicts are Append (add to an existing section), Revise (existing content is inaccurate, propose a correction), New Section, New File, Already Covered (covered even if worded differently), and Too Specific (should stay at the skill level). Each verdict refers to a different remediation path. Append is the most common outcome on mature rule sets.

## What are the three workflow phases?

The three phases are Inventory (Glob enumerates skills and reads all rule files), Cross-read & Verdict (the skill reads all skills plus the full rules text in one context and emits candidates), and User Review (summary table, then one candidate at a time with evidence, violation risk and draft, answered `[y/n/skip]`; bulk approval is banned). Phase 2 is the load-bearing one, and it runs in a single context rather than batched subagents.

## What is the anti-abstraction safeguard?

The safeguard refers to six tests applied during candidate extraction. A principle is included only when all six hold: it is environment-specific (a fact, wiring or trap of this machine, harness or accounts), the model does not already do it, it is not a procedure (steps belong in a skill), it is actionable as a do-X or don't-do-Y rule, it carries a clear violation risk statable in one sentence, and it is not already in rules. Recurrence across skills is reported as evidence, not a gate, so a one-off environment trap can pass. The tests counter the LLM's tendency to abstract every observation into a rule.

## What is the "Glob = exhaustive collection, LLM = judgment" principle?

The principle refers to splitting the workflow into a deterministic part and a judgment part. Glob guarantees no skill or rule file is missed — it enumerates skill definition files exhaustively and excludes dependency markdown structurally. The LLM is the judgment layer that cross-reads the full context. Neither alone is sufficient — Glob cannot judge semantic overlap, and an LLM cannot guarantee exhaustiveness without a deterministic enumerator.

## Why no batching, and why was the cross-batch merge removed?

Earlier versions grouped skills into thematic clusters, analyzed each cluster in a separate subagent, then ran a cross-batch merge. That merge existed only to recover the "appears in 2+ skills" signal that batching broke — a principle found in one skill per batch but two skills overall had to be reassembled afterward. With a large context window the whole corpus fits in one context, so the recurrence count is exact from the start and no merge step is needed, and seeing the full rules text next to all skills makes the "not already in rules" test reliable. Removing batching both simplifies the skill and makes its judgments more accurate.

## When should I NOT use this skill?

Not on a fresh installation with fewer than ten skills — the cost of evaluation exceeds the value of consolidation at small scale. It is a consolidation tool, not an authoring tool; authors new to rule writing benefit more from writing rules manually than from auto-promotion. It also requires a rules directory to exist; pure skill collections with no rules cannot use it.

## How does this skill relate to skill auditing?

Skill auditing tools (e.g. skill-stocktake) audit per-skill quality, while this skill promotes environment-specific principles found in skills into the rules layer. Run stocktake first, then distill what survives. rules-stocktake covers the reverse direction over the same boundary: it audits the rules this skill produces and demotes back what stopped earning its always-loaded slot. Together they cover within-layer audit and cross-layer promotion and demotion.

## Who is shimo4228?

shimo4228 is the author; the hub (https://github.com/shimo4228/shimo4228) lists five practice lines, including the three agent-design lines listed in Project Facts above: AKC — a six-phase bidirectional growth loop; Contemplative Agent — agents grounded in four contemplative axioms; and AAP — harness-neutral accountability ADRs. This skill is scaffolding for the **Promote** phase of AKC.
